Unleash your imagination and start your engines! Based on a movement system called OktagonSystem©, Vektorace can be played on any flat surface, adapting from time to time to your needs. Each game involves the creation of a new race course and only your “vector driving” experience will allow you to win! The basic rules can be learned in a few minutes and immediately you can get behind the wheel for a “sprint” race For simplicity, the BGA implementation uses the tournament map "Indianottolis", with its four variants, as the only reference for the racing track. The ruleset of this implementation refer to the 2nd edition of the game (2022). Number of players: 2 - 6 Game duration: 45 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play VektoRace and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Race around a track. First one to the finish line wins. Movement is via "rulers" of different lengths, depending on the gear your car is in. You place the ruler at the front of your car, then your car is moved to the end of the ruler. At the beginning of the race you choose a combination of tokens which you spend during the race to speed up or slow down/drift. You can get more tokens by pitting. [Rating: 4/10] Vektorace starts with a good promise of racing using templates and customizable tracks, but in practice I found none of it materializes. The driving mechanics remind me of Gaslands but there's practically no risk, so I found that in most turns there were no choices to make, other than the most obvious one: keep moving forward. The cars were so spread apart from the start that there was no meaningful interaction between them. [Rating: 5/10] Nice concept and good components. Like most racing games, it´s much slower than a race. Like most tabletop miniature games, you need to agree on how precise you need to be in handling the pieces. Not a game I´m keen to play again, but I could be talked into it. Despite my rating of 5, if you are at all interested, I really think you should give it a try. Our race saw a nice development, with cool and realistic situations.

[Rating: 5/10] It's no Rallyman GT.  A racer harking back to the old printed grid and pen style racers and the likes of Bolide.  However this time around the board has been ditched, and replaced with over engineered, gimmicky, hex shaped cardboard cars and rulers.  Still a dull vector game at heart.

[Rating: 5/10] In my imagination this was a racing game design I had imagined making myself many years ago when I first played X-Wing but I never got around to making a prototype, so I was excited to finally get to try this octagon-based interpretation.  In practice, it wasn't very exciting - it felt very procedural, difficult to pass cars, and you're too often blocked.  Being able to spend a nitro to jump ahead if you get right up against a car feels odd, but is the only way to get ahead really unless a player makes a mistake.
